name: v1.6.0 — layered connectivity diagnostics
body:
"curl failed" is not a diagnosis. This release rebuilds the Network screen around
that idea: instead of one probe at a time and a pass/fail light, it walks the network
stack bottom-up and tells you *which layer* broke — which is the difference between
fixing something and guessing at it. Four one-click checks, per-host targets in
`probes.yml`, and every tool's verbatim output kept on screen next to the verdict.

## Added

**Run all — a five-rung connectivity ladder.** Link, gateway, internet, DNS, HTTPS,
streamed a line at a time, ending in a verdict that names the *lowest* thing that
broke. Every rung runs even after one fails, deliberately: halting at the first
failure would confidently report "gateway down" on any cloud host whose gateway
simply drops ICMP. The rungs above a failure are what tell you whether that failure
actually mattered.

**Traceroute and TCP port checks.** `Trace` prefers `traceroute`, falls back to
`tracepath`, and prints the `apt install` line if neither is present. Partial hops
survive a timeout, so a path that goes dark still shows you how far it got. `Port`
resolves the name first so a DNS failure never masquerades as a connection timeout.

**Nameserver facts up front.** The Checks tab opens with interface, address, gateway,
link state, and the nameservers from `/etc/resolv.conf` — flagging a `127.0.0.53`
systemd-resolved stub and pointing at `resolvectl status`, since the real upstreams
sit behind it.

**`probes.yml` for per-host targets.** Targets and timing for every probe, under
`~/.config/fleetfix/probes.yml`. Target *lists* replace the built-ins while scalar
knobs *merge* — a deliberate asymmetry, because a fleet's inventory is a replacement
and a timeout is a tuning. Every numeric is clamped to a sane range and bad YAML
degrades per-field to defaults with a logged warning, so no misconfiguration can stop
the Network screen from opening.

**`warn` as a real tier.** Not a softened failure. A 4xx means the server answered, so
the whole path under it works. A refused TCP port means the host answered and nothing
is listening — a service problem, not a path problem. A traceroute going dark mid-path
is usually ICMP-rate-limited transit and says nothing about the destination.

## Fixed

**Ladder rungs no longer fail on evidence from the wrong layer.** Two rungs graded
something other than the layer they represent, either of which could hand a healthy
host a confident "this layer is broken" verdict — and because the verdict names the
lowest failure, either one stole the headline from the rungs that actually measured
something. The link rung failed on anything that was not exactly `operstate == "up"`,
but `unknown` is what wireguard, tun/tap and carrier-less virtio links report *while
passing traffic*, and it is also the sysfs reader's own fallback on error; only `down`
fails now. The HTTPS rung inherited the standalone curl probe's 2xx/3xx definition of
success, so pointing `ladder.https_url` at an auth-gated health endpoint reported
"https is the lowest thing broken" on a box whose entire path worked; any status code
now passes that rung, while real transport failures still fail it.

**Superseded probe results can no longer land.** Cancelling a Textual worker does not
interrupt an OS thread already inside a subprocess, so a slow probe could return after
a newer one and overwrite it. A generation counter, checked on the UI thread at apply
time, drops results from any worker that has been superseded.

## Install

```sh
curl -LO https://github.com/KingPin/FleetFix/releases/download/v1.6.0/fleetfix-linux-x86_64
curl -LO https://github.com/KingPin/FleetFix/releases/download/v1.6.0/fleetfix-linux-x86_64.sha256
sha256sum -c fleetfix-linux-x86_64.sha256
chmod +x fleetfix-linux-x86_64
sudo install -m 0755 fleetfix-linux-x86_64 /usr/local/bin/fleetfix
```

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/KingPin/FleetFix/compare/v1.5.0...v1.6.0
